sources.title: George Lusztig, Hecke Algebras with Unequal Parameters, revised arXiv text (2014)

contents.name: Weight functions and the odd-edge condition
contents.reason: The item defines the ordered group algebra and weight function; the adjacent lemma proves the odd-edge criterion and extension directly.

contents.name: Unequal-parameter Hecke presentation and standard basis
contents.reason: The local definition fixes the symmetric quadratic normalization and finite braid relations.

contents.name: Bar involution and triangular Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
contents.reason: The local proof supplies the full ordered-group induction and uniqueness argument rather than treating Lusztig's statement as a substitute proof.

contents.name: Weighted left, right, and two-sided cells and their quotients
contents.reason: The local definition adopts the coefficient-transition convention and the module theorem proves ideal closure directly.

contents.name: Boundedness and the status of P1–P15
contents.reason: The remark records Lusztig's exact boundedness convention and preserves P1–P15 as conjectures in the general bounded setup.

contents.name: General positivity, semisimplicity, and irreducible classification
contents.reason: No such general property is asserted; the theorem proves only quotient-module well-definedness and its cell-indexed basis.

sources.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras, EPFL lecture notes (2006)
sources.locator: §4.1, especially Theorem 4.11, Definition 4.13, Remark 4.14 and Example 4.15, PDF pp. 15–24; full relevant section inspected.

contents.name: Generic trace expansion and Schur elements
contents.reason: The item defines Schur elements by the irreducible-character expansion of a symmetrizing trace and computes the rank-one coefficients in the A1×A1 proof.

contents.name: The exact nonzero-Schur-element condition for identity decomposition
contents.reason: The proof computes all four Schur elements and checks that each specializes to 4, which is nonzero at every odd residue characteristic.

contents.name: Canonical basic-set multiplicity and alpha conditions
contents.reason: The definition gives the two triangularity conditions relative to a specified decomposition matrix and integer-valued statistic.

contents.name: A separate type-G2 specialization with no canonical basic set
contents.reason: Geck's example is not identified with the local A1×A1 characteristic-two computation; only the source boundary is retained.

contents.name: Unequal-parameter KL properties outside proved regimes
contents.reason: The local remark preserves the source's warning that general KL and cell properties remain conjectural in some regimes.

sources.title: Anders Björner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups, GTM 231 (2005)
sources.locator: Chapter 1, §§1.4–1.5, printed pp. 17–20; Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.2, printed pp. 27–35; full relevant proofs inspected.

contents.name: Matsumoto connectivity and reduced expressions
contents.reason: The proof uses braid connectivity to show that the sum of simple labels is independent of the reduced word.

contents.name: Finite-generator support, standard parabolics, and subword order
contents.reason: The local theorem transfers these finite-generator results to arbitrary rank by finite normal-closure support.

contents.name: Coxeter systems and reduced words
contents.reason: The local definition records the presentation, word length, reflections, and reflection-chain order used by the proof graph.

contents.name: Type-A cell classification or a general unequal-parameter representation classification
contents.reason: The local result does not import a type-A classification or claim any irreducible-module classification.

sources.locator: §§3.1, 5.1–5.2, 7.4–7.6 and 8.1–8.8, PDF pp. 22–29 and 32–38; full relevant sections inspected.

contents.name: Weighted rank-two KL elements and quadratic products
contents.reason: The example expands the KL products from the stated I2(4) quadratic relations and verifies each displayed transition directly.

contents.name: Weighted cell transition convention
contents.reason: The diagram labels an arrow by left multiplication and does not claim a complete cell classification.

contents.name: General P1–P15 consequences in arbitrary unequal-parameter systems
contents.reason: The B2 calculation establishes only four listed transitions and does not infer conjectural general cell properties.

contents.name: A1×A1 weighted cell characters used before modular reduction
contents.reason: The counterexample recomputes the KL products, cell transitions, and one-dimensional character values locally.

sources.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras, EPFL lecture notes (2006)
sources.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.11, Definition 4.13, Remark 4.14 and Example 4.15, PDF pp. 15 and 22–24; full relevant section inspected.

contents.name: Decomposition matrices and canonical basic-set conditions
contents.reason: The local counterexample computes its own four-row, one-column decomposition matrix and limits its conclusion to label collapse.

contents.name: Geck's distinct type-G2 example where a canonical basic set fails
contents.reason: The A1×A1 example is not presented as Geck's type-G2 counterexample and makes no basic-set nonexistence claim.

contents.name: Reduced dihedral words and finite Bruhat subwords
contents.reason: The proof verifies reducedness and the lower Bruhat support needed to identify C_st and C_ts.
